name: Weekly digest
description: Batches a period's activity into one message — figures first, then grouped lists — so the per-event notifications behind it can be switched off.

origin.note: Design: dashboard digest — a boxed figure row over grouped rule-separated lists, closing on a tinted band that treats the frequency control as an offer rather than as fine print.

subject: {{ digest_title }}, {{ period_label }}
preheader: Everything from the period in one message, grouped, with a way to make it arrive less often.

digest_title.description: What the reader calls this thing when it lands. Keep it the same every send — a digest earns its place by being recognisable in a list of unread mail.

period_label.description: The window this covers, stated exactly. A digest that does not say what it covers cannot be trusted to be complete, which is the only thing it is selling.

digest_summary.description: One line separating what happened from what needs the reader. Written by you, not counted by the template, because "two of these need you" is a judgement.
digest_summary.example: Nine things happened. Two are waiting on you.

stats.description: Two or three figures for the period, each with `value`, `label` and an optional `caption` carrying the comparison that makes the figure mean anything. Four fit; three read.

groups.description: The activity itself, grouped by what it is rather than when it happened — each entry a `title` and a list of `items`, and each item a `text` with an optional `detail` line under it. Grouping is the whole reason a digest beats nine separate emails.

empty_text.description: What the digest says when the period was genuinely quiet. Sending it anyway keeps the rhythm and proves the digest is not broken, so this line has to make a quiet week feel deliberate.
empty_text.default: Nothing needed you this period. The digest still arrives on schedule, so an empty one means quiet rather than broken.

action_label.description: Label on the action under the lists. It is an overflow route for anything the digest summarised too briefly, not the point of the email.

action_url.description: Where the full activity lives for anyone who wants more than the summary.

frequency_title.description: Heading on the closing band. This template exists so per-event mail can be switched off, so the switch gets a heading of its own.

frequency_text.description: The offer, in plain terms: this message replaces the individual notifications, and it can arrive more or less often. State it every time — the reader has forgotten what they chose.
frequency_text.default: This digest stands in for the individual notifications behind everything listed above. It can arrive daily, weekly, monthly, or not at all.

frequency_label.description: Label on the outlined button in that band. Offer the change, not the settings screen.

notification_settings_url.description: Where the frequency actually gets changed. Required rather than optional here: a batched message that offers no way out is how a digest turns into a spam report.
